chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Asbaat, from a mawla (freedman/companion) of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from the people of Medina, who said:
I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) ascend Al-Marwa, so he attached himself upon the rock which was at the top part of the pathway, and faced the Kabah.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (a title for Imam Al-Hasan ibn Ali, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحَجَر: The rock (specifically the marker rock at the top of Marwa)
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Kaaba (the cubic building at the center of the Great Mosque in Mecca)
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwa (the hill/pathway in Mecca where pilgrims walk between Safa and Marwa)

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette of pausing and supplicating during the Sa'i ritual at Al-Marwa?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* provides a specific *fiqh* precedent for the etiquette of *Du'a* during *Sa'i*, illustrating Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) pausing at the summit of Al-Marwa to face the Kaaba. In Shia jurisprudence, this physical posture is often interpreted as a sign of humility and focused devotion, reinforcing the spiritual dimension of the ritual movement between Safa and Marwa. The act of leaning against the stone while facing the House of God underscores the connection between physical action and spiritual presence (*Hudur al-Qalb*).
